text:
/ Markets Caterpillar's Rise Is No Longer Enough to Support Dow, Blue Chip Index Falls Caterpillar started the day off in the green, dipped into the red, and is back in the green. The Dow was matching its every move, but is now declining independently. Jul30,201811:47AMEDT The Monday Market Minute Caterpillar was leading the Dow higher following its second-quarter earnings release, but the stock is now showing volatility The Dow is looking for its fourth daily gain in five sessions Meanwhile the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are both trying to hold on for the fourth straight monthly gain. Market Snapshot
Stronger-than-expected earnings from Caterpillar Inc. ( CAT ) helped send the Dow Jones Industrial Average higher after the group posted forecast-busting profits and boosted its full year guidance, as the heavy equipment maker looks to have surpassed its own "high water mark" for future profits despite rising input costs and the threat of tariffs on exports into some of its key markets.
However, Caterpillar shares have spent time in both positive and negative territory Monday, leading to volatility in the Dow.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 0.24%, or 62 points to 25,389, while the S&P 500 lost 0.4%, or 11 points. The Nasdaq , is down 1.1%, or 84 points.
Caterpillar shares are up 1.33% to $144.46 Monday.
Facebook Inc.'s ( FB ) $119 billion slide last week , along with sub-par quarterly results from FAANG member Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ) and chipmaker Intel Corp. ( INTC ) , put investors on the defensive heading into the end of the week on Wall Street, even as forecast-smashing numbers from Amazon Inc. ( AMZN ) steadied nerves and suggested a modest decoupling of stocks in a sector that has driven the lion's share of U.S. equity market gains this year.
Corporate earnings are set to grow at 22.7%, the second-fastest pace in the past eight years, bested only by the 23% advance recorded over the first three months of the year as the broader economy records its best GDP growth since mid-2014.
"I don't think this is a one- or two-year phenomenon. I think we definitely are in a period of four or five years of sustained 3 percent growth at least," U.S. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin told Fox News Sunday. US GDP rose by 4.1% SAAR in Q2, or 2.8% y/y. That's the fastest rate of growth in 3 years. I've never really understood why so many have been so bearish on the US economy for so long. Hopefully also economists are "marked-to market". pic.twitter.com/Bwsjl5DCcX — Teis Knuthsen (@TeisKnuthsen) July 30, 2018
Investors won't have to wait long to find out if tech will continue to drive near-term sentiment , however, with Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) set to report its fiscal third quarter earnings after the close of trading on Tuesday. FactSet estimates suggest the Cupertino, Calif.-based group to report Q3 EPS of $2.16 per share, a 29% increase from the same period last year, on sales of $52.3 billion.
The iphone maker's update comes amid another busy week for corporate reporting, with earnings expected from 140 companies listed on the S&P 500 including Lowe's ( L ) . Pfizer Inc. ( PFE ) , Proctor & Gamble Co. ( PG ) , Telsa Inc. ( TSLA ) , CBS Corp. ( CBS ) and Warren Buffet's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. ( BRK.A ) Register for the Free 'Morning Jolt' Daily Newsletter
Global stocks drifted lower Monday, with tech shares weighing down benchmarks in Europe and Asia following a series of disappointing earnings from some key names in the so-called FAANG complex last week that could test market growth prospects in the second half of the year.
Tech stocks kept Asian markets in check throughout most of the session, pushing the region-wide MSCI Asia ex-Japan index 0.39% lower heading into the close while Japan's Nikkei 225 shed 0.74% to end the day at 22,544.84 points. Tencent Holdings ( TCEHY ) fell 2.68% on China's CSI 300 while Alibaba Group Holdings ( BABA ) was marked 2.45% lower heading into the closing bell. Baidu Inc. ( BIDU ) was also notably lower, falling 2% in China trading to trim its year-to-date gain to just over 7%.
